name: Gianni Agnelli
role: Italian industrialist, Fiat chairman (1966–1996) and senator for life (1991–2003)
summary: Agnelli advocated open markets, European monetary and political integration, and Atlantic cooperation. He favored reforming costly welfare arrangements while supporting international development assistance and managed immigration; his labor relations combined negotiated cooperation with efforts to curb union power at Fiat.

unions-good.rationale: He negotiated major union agreements but subsequently backed reducing union influence within Fiat.

cut-welfare.rationale: He calls for welfare reform because excessive social spending undermines employment and investment; dependency is not his stated argument.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He favors managing migration and investing in reception and integration, opposing sealed borders.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He demands greater capacity for international institutions to manage global problems.

free-trade.rationale: He explicitly advocates worldwide trade liberalization as a source of prosperity.

nation-first.rationale: He says national protection requires international cooperation and continued integration.

open-borders.rationale: He explicitly rejects indiscriminate border opening as simplistic.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He rejects European protectionism as harmful to prosperity and employment.

democracy-best.rationale: He explicitly affirms the superiority of democratic government.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He endorses replacing conquest and domination with international cooperation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He advocates fiscal consolidation but later praises temporary countercyclical budget flexibility after September 11.

class-collaboration.rationale: His producer pact proposes labor-capital cooperation against unproductive rents.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He calls for Europe to become a stronger unified political actor.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He praises the Atlantic integration that brought Italy into NATO.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He urges wealthy governments to increase resources for development infrastructure and education.

common-currency.rationale: He strongly advocates implementing the euro on schedule.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He rejects closing Europe to outside commerce.

delink-world-market.rationale: He favors participation in global markets rather than isolation.

defeat-communism.rationale: He opposes Soviet-bloc domination while explicitly pursuing peaceful East-West coexistence and commerce.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He welcomes Italy’s Western alignment and rejects joining the Soviet bloc.

capital-controls.rationale: He promotes global liberalization of goods, services and capital.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He signed the 1975 national wage-indexation agreement and defended restoring order to collective bargaining.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He defends Maastricht constraints as supports for European monetary integration.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He demands rich-country market access for poorer exporters and health exceptions to patents.

notes: No inferred answers. Reviewed all statement themes and remaining nulls. Social, ecological and technological positions are not inferred from his occupation, family, private life or business products. The 1997 conference contains many speakers: only Agnelli’s own intervention between its introduction and the moderator’s thanks is used. Welfare retrenchment is qualified because he criticized costs, not explicitly personal dependency. Opposition to communist bloc rule is distinguished from hostility to all coexistence with communist states. Full texts downloaded and searched where direct retrieval succeeded; the Senate PDF was read through the web tool after direct download was blocked.
